extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedy screenwriters, film writers, and filmmakers seeking practical guidance on writing comedy films
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting comedic feature films and screenplays, covering the mechanics of humor, principles that make things funny, developing a comic voice, and the structures/requirements of many comedy subgenres.

rubrics_metrics.name: learn the successful mechanics and characteristics of various comic story forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Book-level objective: discover what makes us laugh and how to craft better comedy by learning the mechanics and characteristics of comic story forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sit down, shut up, and split a gut
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter/title (imperative): implied emphasis on getting to the point and making the audience laugh; a headline for an approach to amusing the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic perspective: how to develop a comic voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing a distinct comic perspective/voice for a piece of comedy; guidance on cultivating a point of view that generates humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: How comedy works: the physics of funny
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles explaining the mechanics behind why things are funny—the 'physics' of how jokes and comedic situations function.

rubrics_metrics.name: The tenets of laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Core principles or rules that underlie laughter and comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy is conflict and collision
rubrics_metrics.description: Position that comedy often arises from conflict and collision between characters, ideas, or situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy is conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that committed character belief or conviction fuels comedic situations and punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy is deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that uses of deception (misdirection, lies, misunderstandings) are a source of comedic payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy is wish-fulfillment and worst fear
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that comedy can play between fulfilling desires and exposing anxieties/fears for humorous effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy is truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that comedy often stems from recognizably true observations about people, situations, or society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy is chaos and anarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that comedic effect can come from disorder, rule-breaking, and anarchic situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy and children
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations for writing comedy involving children or for child-centered comedic perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic stories and their structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on structural elements specific to comic storytelling—how comedic stories are built and paced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fish-out-of-water
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: comedic scenarios based on a character placed in an unfamiliar environment; structural and mechanistic guidance for this comic type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: principles, beats, and mechanics specific to romantic comedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: The sports comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: mechanics and characteristics particular to comedies set around sports.

rubrics_metrics.name: The crime/caper comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: guidance for comedic stories centered on crime, heists, or capers.

rubrics_metrics.name: The military comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: principles and comic devices used in military-set comedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: The teen/coming-of-age comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: structure and comic mechanics for teen-focused or coming-of-age comedic narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: The ensemble comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: writing and structuring comedies that rely on an ensemble cast and interlocking character dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farce
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: the conventions, timing, and exaggerated situations characteristic of farce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: using dark, taboo, or morbid subjects for comedic effect; tonal and ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire, parody and mockumentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/form: approaches to satirical comedy, parody, and mockumentary formats, including targets, techniques, and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: The end of the laughter?
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion/essay-style chapter title likely about changing trends, limits, or future of comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A. the stages of the hero's journey
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource: mapping the stages of the hero's journey (story structure) as an appendix resource applicable to comedic storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B. AFI's 100 years, 100 laughs
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource: a canonical list (AFI's '100 laughs') provided as a reference for influential comedic moments/films.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix C. Top ten comedies from the past five years
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource: recent notable comedies listed as reference/examples for study.
